title: Treasury December coupon announcement — the 3-Year new issue, the 10-Year and 30-Year REOPENINGS and three bills, for the block that straddles the 12-09 FOMC
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes, PDF CreationDate 2026-08-04), FlateDecode streams inflated per page and rows rebuilt from Tm coordinates. SIX rows carry the announce date `Thursday, December 03, 2026`: `13-Week BILL` and `26-Week BILL` (auction Mon 12-07, settle Thu 12-10), `6-Week BILL` (auction Tue 12-08, settle Thu 12-10), `3-Year NOTE` — no `R`, a new issue — (auction Mon 12-07, settle Tue 12-15), `10-Year NOTE / R` (auction Tue 12-08, settle Tue 12-15) and `30-Year BOND / R` (auction Thu 12-10, settle Tue 12-15). 11:00am ET is Treasury's standing coupon-announcement convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the single proposal that seeded it (proposals/treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-03.from-treasury-3y-note-2026-12-07.json) in full first. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THAT PROPOSAL, both derived this session from api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov auctions_query rather than inherited. (1) COMPOSITION: SIX securities, not the three the proposal named — the 13-Week, 26-Week and 6-Week bills carry the same `Thursday, December 03, 2026` announce date on page 3 of the same PDF. (2) SIZES: the proposal wrote `Expect $58B/$42B/$25B`, which are the NEW-ISSUE sizes. The schedule flags the 10-Year and 30-Year with `R`, and every reopening in the modern grid runs below its own new issue: 10-Year reopening $39B for 21 consecutive auctions since 2024-03-12, 30-Year reopening $22B for 21 consecutive since 2024-03-13, zero deviations in either. The correct expectations are $58B / $39B / $22B, and the August 2026 refunding statement sb0590's own table displays exactly that split twice (its Jun-26 and Sep-26 rows read `... 39 13 22`). WHAT THIS ANNOUNCEMENT SETTLES: it publishes the December CUSIPs, of which only the 3-Year's is genuinely unknowable in advance — the 3-Year is a new issue every month (`reopening: "No"` on all 45 rows since 2023), while the 10-Year and 30-Year reopen the November refunding's own securities. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: the coupon sizes, which the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding sets 29 days earlier (sb0590 names that date in writing: `The next quarterly refunding announcement will take place on Wednesday, November 4, 2026`). STRUCTURAL: a Thursday announce date is the mid-quarter tell — refunding announcements are Wednesday 15 of 15 since 2023, mid-quarter ones Thursday 29 of 30, the single exception 2024-07-03 displaced by Independence Day. Symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
